entry.evidence: more research is needed to select an appropriate tracer for mixing zone delimitation in tropical marine waters

sequences.source_document: Published paper PDF and publisher XML text

steps.action: After reviewing tracer studies at outfalls, the authors ask whether uranine can delimit a mixing zone in non-stratified tropical water, using the Cartagena outfall as the case.
steps.quote: the current study evaluates the use of uranine (sodium fluorescein) as a tracer for the delimitation of a mixing zone

steps.action: Tracer properties of uranine (low detection limit, insensitive to salinity, photostable, non-toxic) are taken from the literature.
steps.quote: uranine is not affected by salinity and is a photostable and non-toxic substance to marine ecosystems

steps.action: The pre-construction model prediction of good outfall performance (Roberts and Villegas 2006) is cited as the prior expectation.
steps.quote: The viability of this system’s implementation was evaluated using mathematical modeling, predicting a good performance of the outfall

steps.action: Currents were measured with buoys and two ADCPs (Nov 2018 to Mar 2019), and the 2013-2019 airport precipitation record was compiled to characterize the discharge area.
steps.quote: The marine current speed and direction were measured using buoys and an acoustic Doppler current profiler (ADCP)

steps.action: The injected uranine concentration was set by a mass balance using injection rate, wastewater flow, a 1:1500 dilution limit and the fluorometer detection limit, and sampling stations were oriented along the measured currents.
steps.quote: The injected uranine concentration at the WWTP was determined based a mass balance

steps.action: Uranine was injected into the live discharge at the Parshall flume in two campaigns (April and December 2019), and the plume was sampled at 11 and 40 stations at four depths.
steps.quote: Two tracer field campaigns were conducted for mixing zone delimitation

steps.action: Uranine was read with a handheld fluorometer, confirmed on a laboratory microplate reader, and calibrated against concentration.
steps.quote: Uranine samples were analyzed using first an AquaFluor handheld fluorometer, and then confirming the results

steps.action: In December, 17 CTD profiles were taken on a 300 m grid, and water samples were analysed for salinity, TSS, fecal coliforms and enterococci by Standard Methods.
steps.quote: During the second field campaign, 17 CTD (conductivity–temperature–depth) profiles were obtained

steps.action: Current speeds (mostly below 0.2 m/s) and the southwestward, coast-parallel direction were compared with Maza et al. (2006) and found to agree.
steps.quote: These results agree with those reported by Maza et al. (2006).

steps.action: The density gradient from the CTD profiles gave a Brunt–Väisälä frequency of 1.3e-2 s^-1, read as an unstratified water column.
steps.quote: This floatability frequency reflected an unstratified marine water column under the study conditions.

steps.action: The unstratified state was checked against drone photographs showing the dyed plume reaching the surface within 100-200 m of the diffuser.
steps.quote: The unstratified marine water conditions were confirmed by considering that the diluted wastewater plume reached the water surface within the first 100–200 m

steps.action: Dilution factors were computed from uranine concentrations (Eq. 1): 754.9 at 1 m and 3.83e4 at 17 m within 30 m of the diffuser, and about 3.7-4.4e4 at 150 m.
steps.quote: The dilution factors, as one of the main submarine outfall efficiency indicators, were estimated based on uranine concentration profiles.

steps.action: The plume-rise and dilution pattern was reported as seen in both seasonal campaigns.
steps.quote: This behavior was also evident in both field campaigns due to the rise of the plume

steps.action: The dilution factors were compared with those reported for the Santa Marta, Boston and Ipanema outfalls.
steps.quote: The dilution factors obtained in this study are in agreement with those obtained by García et al. (2013)

steps.action: Fecal coliform and enterococci distributions were mapped by depth: 56% of coliform samples failed the primary-contact limit, and enterococci peaked at 1 m.
steps.quote: On this basis, 44% of the samples indicated compliance for primary contact and 56% did not meet this criterion.

steps.action: The enterococci depth distribution was used as an independent check that the plume rose to the surface, as the uranine contours showed.
steps.quote: it is again confirmed that the plume rose to the surface, as drawn from the uranine contours analysis.

steps.action: The regulatory mixing zone was delimited in ArcGIS as a quadrilateral where enterococci exceed 100 CFU/100 mL at 1 m: 6.61 km2, extending up to 1.67 km.
steps.quote: the mixing zone obtained had a quadrilateral shape with a perimeter of 10.6 km

steps.action: The estimated mixing-zone extent was compared with international guideline limits of 100-1000 m and found to exceed them.
steps.quote: exceeds the maximum limits established between 100 and 1000 m by most of the regulated countries

steps.action: The mixing zone was re-derived with fecal coliforms (200 MPN limit), giving a similar 6.11 km2 area.
steps.quote: Here, the region is very similar to the one obtained with enterococci

steps.action: Uranine was compared with the microbiological indicators by correlation and PCA (53% with enterococci, 46% with coliforms), and plume shapes were compared.
steps.quote: this indicator had a good relationship with the tracer because uranine was able to explain 53% of the enterococci behavior

steps.action: Because the detectable tracer plume was far smaller than the microbiological mixing zone, the authors recommend a much higher injected uranine concentration and more sampling points.
steps.quote: the initial uranine injected at the WWTP should be much higher than the used in this study

steps.action: The claim is kept that uranine is suitable for delimiting and visualizing the wastewater mixing zone in tropical marine waters.
steps.quote: Uranine is suitable for delimiting the wastewater mixing zone in tropical marine waters.

tree.answer: Wastewater plume mixing and dilution around the Cartagena outfall diffuser
Partly; plume traced by an injected fluorescent dye, microbiological indicators and drone images
Evaluate uranine as a tracer and delimit the regulatory mixing zone
No rival explanations; alternative tracers and models dismissed from the literature
Conditions found in the live discharge during two field campaigns
Partly; coliform and enterococci zones agree, and drone/enterococci confirm the unstratified plume rise, but the tracer plume is much smaller than the zone
Uranine judged suitable; mixing zone 6.6 km2

end.claim: Uranine is suitable for delimiting the wastewater mixing zone of a submarine outfall in non-stratified tropical marine water, with dilution up to 1:43000 within 150 m and a regulatory mixing zone of 6.6 km2 at Cartagena.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the two uranine injections into the live outfall discharge, with plume sampling at several depths, there would be no tracer concentrations, dilution factors or tracer-based mixing zone.

gates.evidence: The aim of evaluating uranine directed the tracer injection and sampling design (p. 5), but no hypothesis with failure criteria was stated. Tracer suitability was compared with the microbiological indicators (correlations of 46-53%) and with drone and CTD evidence (pp. 9, 12); no threshold for 'suitable' was set, and the tracer plume (2521 m2) fell far short of the 6.6 km2 zone, yet suitability was still asserted. The injection concentration (mass balance) and the regulatory thresholds (100 CFU/100 mL, 200 MPN/100 mL) were fixed before sampling (pp. 5-6).

Fluorometry with a handheld fluorometer and a laboratory microplate reader (Thermo Scientific Varioskan LUX)

novelty_claims.quote: a detailed study of the effluent dilution and transport processes had not been carried out after the submarine outfall implementation
uranine has been used in tropical areas but only in stratified marine waters
In Colombia, there is not yet a specific methodology for mixing zone delimitation

limits: The XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body steps are located by PDF page. Sub-claims and their statuses: water column unstratified (estimate_with_resolution, from one December CTD survey only); dilution factors up to 4.36e4 (estimate_with_resolution, with no uncertainty given); mixing zone 6.61 km2 by enterococci and 6.11 km2 by coliforms (estimate_with_resolution, spatially interpolated in ArcGIS with no interpolation error reported). The claim that both seasons gave similar dilutions is not backed by separate April numbers in the text. The abstract gives temperature 29.0-29.35 °C, the body 29-29.2 °C. The tracer plume area (2521 m2) and perimeter (6401 m) are geometrically inconsistent. Whether the reported correlations (92%, 53%, 46%) are r or R² is unclear. Uranine 'suitability' is asserted although the detectable tracer plume covered only a small fraction of the indicator-defined zone; inference: suitability is a qualitative judgment. No criterion for tracer success was registered. Detail of the April campaign (11 stations, 1 h injection) is sparse. Tracer decay was said to be evaluated, but no decay result is reported. No review file was supplied.

disagreements.target: Rhodamine WT as an outfall tracer (e.g., Hunt et al. 2010)
disagreements.support: Cites genotoxicity and fish-embryo toxicity studies (Dieter et al. 2001; Skjolding et al. 2021); no new evidence.
disagreements.quote: [...] been demonstrated to be genotoxic in mice and Salmonella typhimurium

disagreements.target: CDOM as an effluent tracer (Nezlin et al. 2020)
disagreements.support: Cites reported fluorometer calibration problems and non-effluent CDOM sources; no new evidence.
disagreements.quote: CDOM studies have revealed problems with fluorometer (calibration and measurements) and non-effluent (unclear) sources of CDOM

disagreements.support: Cites high model uncertainty and calibration data needs (European Commission 2010; Pecly and Roldão 2011), motivating a field tracer approach.
disagreements.quote: the disadvantages include high uncertainty due to the mathematical and numerical models

disagreements.support: The field-delimited Cartagena zone extends up to 1.67 km, beyond most guideline limits, so the authors argue microbiological standards need complete field studies.
disagreements.quote: exceeds the maximum limits established between 100 and 1000 m by most of the regulated countries

alternatives_considered.reason: Rhodamine WT toxicity, CDOM fluorometer and source problems, fast ammonia transformation; uranine has a low detection limit, is non-toxic and is not affected by salinity
High uncertainty of models and their calibration and validation data needs

alternatives_considered.chosen: Enterococci at 1 m (100 CFU/100 mL) as headline mixing-zone indicator
alternatives_considered.reason: Enterococci are more resistant to saline media and correlate better with uranine

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Circles or semicircles (Canada, UK, Brazil, Peru guidelines); irregular shapes (USA)
